theory: A tube closed at the bottom by water has a node at the water surface and an antinode just beyond the open mouth. The air column resonates when its effective length is an odd number of quarter wavelengths.

Subtracting removes the end correction $e$: $l_2 - l_1 = \dfrac{\lambda}{2} = \dfrac{v}{2f}$, so a graph of $(l_2 - l_1)$ against $1/f$ is a straight line through the origin with slope $v/2$. Each pair also gives $e = \dfrac{l_2 - 3l_1}{2}$.
The speed of sound rises with temperature, $v = 331.3\sqrt{1 + \theta/273}$ m s⁻¹, so the result is corrected to 0 °C with $v_0 = v\sqrt{\dfrac{273}{273 + \theta}}$.

apparatus.tube: Resonance tube: a glass tube on a retort stand, joined to a water reservoir by rubber tubing.
apparatus.reservoir: Reservoir: raising or lowering it sets the water level in the tube.
apparatus.forks: Set of tuning forks, 256–512 Hz, and a rubber pad.
apparatus.rule: Metre rule beside the tube, reading 0 cm at the mouth.
apparatus.thermometer: Thermometer to measure the air temperature.

safety: Clamp the tube firmly; glass tubes break if knocked.
Mop up spilt water at once.
steps: Raise the water almost to the top of the tube.
Strike a fork on the rubber pad and hold it over the mouth of the tube.
Lower the water slowly until the sound is loudest: read the length l₁ from the mouth to the water surface.
Keep lowering until the sound is loudest again: read l₂.
Repeat with each fork whose second resonance fits in the tube.
Work out l₂ − l₁, 1/f and e = (l₂ − 3l₁)/2. Plot (l₂ − l₁) against 1/f.
tips: Strike the fork again each time: the resonance is only clear while the fork is loud.
Read the bottom of the meniscus with your eye level with the water (Eye level view).
The second resonance of the lowest forks may be below the bottom of the tube.
references: Young, H. D. & Freedman, R. A. University Physics, ch. 16: Sound and hearing (standing waves in pipes).

theory: A tube closed at the bottom by water first resonates when the air column, with its end correction $e$, is a quarter of a wavelength long:
A graph of $l$ against $1/f$ is a straight line with slope $v/4$ and intercept $-e$ on the $l$-axis. For an unflanged tube $e \approx 0.6r$, where $r$ is the internal radius.
Correct the result to 0 °C with $v_0 = v\sqrt{\dfrac{273}{273 + \theta}}$.

apparatus.tube: Resonance tube: a glass tube on a retort stand, joined to a water reservoir by rubber tubing.
apparatus.reservoir: Reservoir: raising or lowering it sets the water level in the tube.
apparatus.forks: Set of tuning forks, 256–512 Hz, and a rubber pad.
apparatus.rule: Metre rule beside the tube, reading 0 cm at the mouth.
apparatus.thermometer: Thermometer to measure the air temperature.

safety: Clamp the tube firmly; glass tubes break if knocked.
Mop up spilt water at once.
steps: Raise the water almost to the top of the tube.
Strike a fork on the rubber pad and hold it over the mouth.
Lower the water slowly until the sound is first loudest: record l (falling).
Lower a little further, then raise the water slowly to the loudest point again: record l (rising).
Work out the mean l and 1/f, then plot l against 1/f.
tips: Start with the water high: the first loud point you meet is the first resonance.
Read the bottom of the meniscus with your eye level with the water (Eye level view).
Your intercept should be negative: it is −e.
references: Young, H. D. & Freedman, R. A. University Physics, ch. 16: Sound and hearing (standing waves in pipes).

noTemperature.title: Record the air temperature
noTemperature.detail: The speed of sound depends on temperature. You need θ to correct your result to 0 °C and to compare it fairly.

secondResonanceRatio.title: l₂ is not about three times l₁
secondResonanceRatio.detail: For the same fork the second resonance is near 3l₁ (a little more, because of the end correction). Check you recorded both resonances of the same fork.

negativeEndCorrection.title: The end correction comes out negative
negativeEndCorrection.detail: e = (l₂ − 3l₁)/2 should be a small positive length (about 0.6 × the tube's radius). Re-check l₁ and l₂.

positiveIntercept.title: Your intercept is positive
positiveIntercept.detail: Because l = v/(4f) − e, the line meets the l-axis at −e, below the origin. Check your line and your 1/f values.

secondNotFirst.title: This length looks like the second resonance
secondNotFirst.detail: It is about three times what the other forks suggest. Start with the water high so the first loud point you meet is the first resonance.
